A mural that was painted in my hometown this week. It's absolutely huge, and the detail is incredible.

How the fuck do you even DO that? I mean, I understand they use a grid system, or projectors to lay out the composition, but how do you DO that exactly? How long does it take? What kind of paint do they use, it has to stand up against the elements and the test of time. What kind of brushes? How do you get permission from the property owner? What are the nuts and bolts of it?

It's part of a mural project that happens every year. There's many large murals all over the city, and obviously, the number grows every year. I've seen them doing them in various stages and they start by sketching it out on a photograph of the building, then they go through some process that I don't know about to scale everything up and apply a wireframe outline on the building. Then using bucket lifts, roller brushes, big, medium, small brushes, and often more than one person helping, the artist just paints it bit by bit. Here's some images of the "girl in a jar" photo I posted in the comments in the process of being made: http://i.imgur.com/2vDlWqQ.png http://i.imgur.com/StFeMoE.jpg Finished product: http://i.imgur.com/arfuWP6.jpg

I think they use a clear protective coating over it (like a polyurethane or something). And it only takes them a few days, depending on how much help they have and their experience. In Richmond, these murals and the mural project are very popular things, and it actually helps raise the property value, especially if the mural is 'famous'.

Absolutely. It's a city that feels like a small town. Very young population due to the growth of Virginia Commonwealth University. Often ranked as one of the best food cities on the east coast. Low cost of living, plenty of jobs whether you're looking for a professional business gig or just an hourly retail job. The James River runs through it and Richmond is located on the river's fall line, making it one of the most gorgeous rivers you'll ever see. If you're a history buff, Richmond has more historical buildings and locations than most entire states. Lots of Civil War historical preserves, even some Revolutionary War and pre-Civil War plantation era sites.

There's a really strong art scene here. Though I'm not personally a fan of most of them, there's a good live music scene and excellent small venues. We're not a sports city, but the Flying Squirrels are a fun minor league baseball team, and in the summer the Washington Redskins have their training camp here which is open to the public. If you're into politics, Richmond is the capital of Virginia, and has a beautiful capitol building that is so old that it served as the design inspiration for the White House and was designed by Thomas Jefferson himself. This is a very interesting time to be in Virginia politics as decades of conservative control are beginning to break down and lots of new things are happening policy-wise. As a life-long Richmond resident, I can say with confidence that Richmond is on the cusp of becoming something very unique in the US. I'm looking forward to seeing where things progress.
